newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Future HK govt to give pension scheme green light.
newsitem.headline: Future HK govt to give pension scheme green light.

text.p: Plans for a massive Hong Kong government pension scheme will suffer no hiccups when the current legislature is dissolved and replaced by a China-backed body on July 1, a senior civil servant said on Tuesday.

"It is everybody's knowlege that one of the key priorities as announced by the chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa is to address our elderly problem," said Rafael Hui, secretary for financial services at a press briefing.

"It is regrettable that all the legislative process cannot be completed in time by our existing legislature," he said, adding no problems were expected when the baton was passed to the next government.
The new parliament will have to take over scrutiny of legislation launching the multi-billion dollar Mandatory Pension Fund plan (MPF).

"From the admininstration's point of view, there is absolute continuity and no break in our work and our legislative process will be completed by the next legislature," said Hui, who will keep the same job under Tung's government.

Annual contributions to the MPF will run into 20 billion Hong Kong dollars in the initial years and that amount could double when the system matures after three decades, Pamela Tan, director of the MPF office, told the press briefing.
The funds will be privately managed, providing huge impetus to the financial sector, Tan said.
"There will be a lot of new opportunities for banks, for trustee companies, for fund management companies as well for the asset custodians," Tan said.
About 10 percent of Hong Kong's population is currently aged 65 and above, and this should increase to about 13 percent in two decades and 20 percent in another two decades, Tan said.
Only one third of Hong Kong's population currently has retirement protection, she noted.
